scores.evidence: Parity check (V8): "Digest must match exactly... SHA-256 of image blobs match bit-for-bit" across old and new platform
scores.rationale: Requiring bit-identical image digests across two different build platforms is unrealistic without reproducible-build work (timestamps, layers), and it gates the cutover; also secret scrubbing of logs is treated as the main secret defense, and "50 concurrent builds; 10 parallel deploys" style numbers are shaky.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 "First end-to-end slice"... pilot "5 pilot services (internal + one external team)" ... "Pilot on-boarding"
scores.rationale: Covers pilot, waves, canary and registry but omits contract testing, service inventory, and the phases include scope creep (multi-cluster, Jaeger, SOC2); the sequencing is largely feasible.

scores.evidence: Phase 5 says "Staging-only cutover" with parity run across all 50, yet Phase 4 "Unlocks: Full platform rollout to all 50 services"
scores.rationale: Mostly consistent overall design but with contradictions: 5 pilot services with 'external team', 10% 'traffic' vs 5 services, Phase 2 signs images yet V3/V4 numbering is inconsistent, and Phase 0 rollback is rerunning a build rather than redeploying.

scores.evidence: V6: "Canary receives 10% traffic; error rate climbs to 6%; controller detects within 30 s; canary is automatically rolled back"
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks (canary abort, RBAC isolation, signing, load) with early checks and measurable criteria, though many thresholds are invented and little post-launch regression validation beyond SLO.

scores.evidence: "ASSUMPTION: shared runner pool; per-team breakdown pending"; "Stateless services dominate"
scores.rationale: Assumptions are labeled in a budget table, but the 5-min latency labeled REQUIREMENT, $8K budget and others are invented, and the language mix and service inventory are not surveyed.

scores.evidence: "Incident severity classification... > 3 critical services fail → kill switch activated"; "unsigned image rejected by admission controller"
scores.rationale: Covers kill switch, canary abort, registry outage, runner crash, but lacks fork PR/untrusted builds, DB migration failures, flaky tests, and pipeline-definition tampering.

scores.evidence: "One platform team, one on-call; runbooks for >95% of alerts"; "burn-rate alerts"; kill-switch tested in drill
scores.rationale: Monitoring, runbooks, rollback, on-call and drills are concrete, though a one-team burden with so many phases (multi-cluster, tracing, SOC2) is heavy.
Cost drivers, attribution, quotas and tiered storage addressed, but figures lack basis and there is no hosted vs self-hosted or build-volume estimate.

scores.evidence: "Reversibility | R3 ... Default (chosen now) ... Revisit trigger"; "Point of no return" decommissioning gate V10
scores.rationale: The plan explicitly rates reversibility, has revisit triggers and a staged decommissioning with grace period, though some ratings are odd and the registry choice is committed early.

scores.evidence: "Phase 7 ... Multi-cluster deployment ... distributed tracing (Jaeger) ... Export for SOC 2 audit"
scores.rationale: Uses existing tools (Tekton, Flagger) but adds speculative multi-cluster, tracing, SOC2 audit log, 9 phases and 11 validation gates for an unstated need.

scores.evidence: "Depends on: Phase 2 (V3, V4 passed)... Exit check: ✓ Build cache hit rate > 60%..."
scores.rationale: Phased with dependencies, concrete tasks and checkable exit criteria per phase, although key items like templates, contract checks and tool choices remain open.

checklist.evidence: "define base image + test command... Store as reusable pipeline templates."
"keeping their old pipeline as fallback; run both for 2 weeks in parallel (parity check)."
"Immutable artifacts + instant switch for stateless"; Image digest deploys but builds are re-done for parity and immutability of tags left as a decision
"Integrate with HashiCorp Vault / AWS Secrets Manager to pull secrets... federated via OIDC" (as option)
"canary is rolled back within 30 s"; no DB migration compatibility
"Build cache hit rate > 60%"; "Code push to test feedback < 5 min p95"
"Size: 5 reserved + up to 25 on-demand"; "cost per build < $0.50"
"One platform team, one on-call; runbooks for >95% of alerts"
"Implement immutable audit log (append-only, cryptographically signed)"; approvals recorded in audit log

traps.evidence: "Wave 2 (50% of services)... Kill-switch mechanism... revert all services to old platform in < 2 min"
"Stores image by digest"; "Every build artifact tagged with build commit SHA"
"per-service service accounts (minimal RBAC)"; "kubeconfig credentials stored in sealed-secret"
"Service-level rollback for individual failures"; per-service deploy config

note: Well-structured, pilot-and-wave migration with measurable gates and a kill switch, but it demands bit-identical cross-platform digests, misses contract testing, fork-PR/OIDC credential handling, and flaky tests, and adds speculative scope.
